1	# WP-004: Queue Type Schema & Entry Normalization
     2	
     3	## Plan Context
     4	
     5	Complete the namespace migration across the entire GUI stack so that no component uses the legacy bare-slug form without the repository namespace prefix, bringing the frontend and orchestrator queue into alignment for multi-root workspace support.
     6	
     7	## Description
     8	
     9	Add the `expectedRepo: string | null` field to the `RawQueueEntry` interface in `types.ts` and add normalization logic in `validate-entry.ts` to set missing `expectedRepo` to `null` for legacy queue entries (so downstream consumers can rely on `string | null`, never `undefined`).
    10	
    11	## Scope
    12	
    13	- `mcp-server/src/gui/queue/types.ts` — `RawQueueEntry` interface (add `expectedRepo` field)
    14	- `mcp-server/src/gui/queue/validate-entry.ts` — normalization of missing `expectedRepo` to `null`
    15	
    16	## Deliverables
    17	
    18	- `RawQueueEntry` interface has a new `expectedRepo: string | null` field
    19	- `isRawQueueEntry()` or `readQueueFile()` in `validate-entry.ts` normalizes missing `expectedRepo` to `null`
    20	- All downstream TypeScript consumers can rely on `expectedRepo` being `string | null` (never `undefined`)
    21	
    22	## Dependencies
    23	
    24	- None
    25	
    26	## Acceptance Criteria
    27	
    28	1. `RawQueueEntry` interface includes `expectedRepo: string | null` field
    29	2. Legacy queue entries (JSON files without `expected_repo`) are normalized to `expectedRepo: null` at the read boundary
    30	3. TypeScript compilation passes with the new field — no type errors in downstream consumers
    31	4. `expectedSlug` retains its original bare-slug semantics (no change to this field)
    32	
    33	## Active Pipeline Stages
    34	
    35	`implementation` → `qa` → `security-audit` → `code-review` → `documentation`
    36	
    37	## Estimated Complexity
    38	
    39	Low
    40	
    41	## Rationale
    42	
    43	A separate `expectedRepo` field eliminates runtime parsing at 4+ consumer sites. The alternative (composite `repo/slug` in `expectedSlug`) would force every reader to detect, split, and fallback — adding one nullable field to a 6-field interface is trivial by comparison.
    44	
    45	## Rejected Approaches
    46	
    47	- **Composite `repo/slug` in `expectedSlug`** — Rejected because it would force every consumer site (4+ locations) to detect the presence of a slash, split the string, and implement fallback logic. A separate nullable field keeps each consumer simple and avoids runtime parsing errors.
    48	
    49	## Notes
    50	
    51	This is the foundation for WP-011 (orchestrator view), WP-007 (queue path resolution), and WP-002 (Python queue registration). It is independent of the frontend view WPs. Phase 3 can proceed in parallel with Phases 1-2.

1	# WP-013: project-detail.js View Migration
     2	
     3	## Plan Context
     4	
     5	Complete the namespace migration across the entire GUI stack so that no component uses the legacy bare-slug form without the repository namespace prefix, bringing the frontend and orchestrator queue into alignment for multi-root workspace support.
     6	
     7	## Description
     8	
     9	Update `project-detail.js` — the largest view file (1045 lines) — to accept `(repo, slug)` in its function signature and all sub-functions (`renderPlan`, `renderSynthesis`), update all API client calls to pass `(repo, slug)`, and update all internal links (WP rows, plan link, synthesis link, run log links).
    10	
    11	## Scope
    12	
    13	- `mcp-server/gui/public/views/project-detail.js` — function signatures, API calls, internal link generation
    14	
    15	## Deliverables
    16	
    17	- `renderProjectDetail(app, repo, slug)` signature updated
    18	- `renderPlan(app, repo, slug)` and `renderSynthesis(app, repo, slug)` signatures updated
    19	- All API calls pass `(repo, slug)` to the namespaced API client methods
    20	- All internal navigation links (WP detail, plan, synthesis, run logs) use `#/projects/{repo}/{slug}/...` form
    21	
    22	## Dependencies
    23	
    24	- WP-001
    25	- WP-008
    26	
    27	## Acceptance Criteria
    28	
    29	1. `renderProjectDetail`, `renderPlan`, and `renderSynthesis` all accept `(app, repo, slug)` signatures
    30	2. Every API call within the view passes `(repo, slug)` to the API client
    31	3. All internal links (WP rows, plan, synthesis, run log links) use the namespaced hash route form
    32	4. No link or API call in the view still uses the bare-slug form
    33	
    34	## Active Pipeline Stages
    35	
    36	`implementation` → `qa` → `code-review` → `documentation`
    37	
    38	## Estimated Complexity
    39	
    40	High
    41	
    42	## Notes
    43	
    44	Depends on WP-001 and WP-008. This is the largest view file at 1045 lines with many internal links and API calls. The high complexity is justified because the changes are mechanically uniform (all the same pattern: add `repo` parameter) — splitting further would create artificial boundaries within a single cohesive view. Test updates in `mcp-server/tests/gui/project-detail-runs.test.ts` are part of the QA pipeline.
